messages:
aj: Heads-up — after enabling the fused dequant->softmax attention kernel for FP8 (e4m3) on the staging cluster, we saw a 12% perf win on long sequences but a 9% regression on short sequences (<32). Also some tiny numeric diffs in token probabilities. Anyone seen similar? :thinking:

kevin: Yep saw that earlier. Short-seq perf loss usually means overhead from the prologue (scale loads / branching) dominates. Did you run with per-channel scales?

aj: Per-head scales (per-channel) on that run. If we switch to per-tensor it helps perf but increases numeric error. The diffs are small but show up on our regression evals.

maria: Two things to check: 1) KV cache alignment effect on vectorized dequant loads (misaligned loads kill perf on some kernels), 2) softmax numeric path when operating in FP16 after dequant — we might need a scaled log-sum-exp stabilization step.

kevin: Agree. Also kernel dispatch overhead — our current registry creates a small lambda per request for dtype routing. For short seqs the lambda + argument marshalling is measurable. Consider a direct ABI entry for common combos (fp8->fp16 fused) so dispatch is a single indirect call.

sara: I'm worried about correctness across variants: fp8-e4m3 vs fp8-e5m2 use different bias/scale semantics. We need a clear contract in the kernel interface for which exponent/format is expected.

aj: Proposal: kernel ABI should include fields: dtype_tag, exponent_format, scale_ptr, scale_layout, kv_alignment_flag. That way the runtime can pick an exact match or fall back. Example registration (pseudo):

```python
register_kernel('attn_dequant_fused', backend='cuda', dtype='fp8', contract={
  'exponent': 'e4m3',
  'requires_kv_alignment': True,
  'scale_ptr': 'float*',
  'scale_layout': 'per_head'
})
```

kevin: That looks reasonable. For fallbacks, prefer: exact kernel -> fp8 dequant-only (no softmax fused) -> fp16 reference path. Runtime should annotate reason for fallback in traces.

maria: Also add a numeric-quality score to kernel metadata (e.g., expected RMS error range), so Optimize/console can flag when a rollout picks a lower-quality kernel.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolling canary: attn_fused_fp8 -> 10% hosts (staging) at 2034567893.

aj: Parallel note — the dequant prologue should avoid per-token branching. Pseudocode: 

```c
// vectorized prologue (simplified)
scale = scale_ptr[head_idx];
for i in 0..len step VEC_SZ:
  fp8_block = load_unaligned(src + i);
  fp16_block = convert_fp8_to_fp16(fp8_block, scale);
  accum_block = matmul_block(fp16_block, ...);
```

sara: For KV-cache interaction: if cache rows are not 16-byte aligned, the load_unaligned path triggers slower codegen on some GPUs. Maybe runtime should attempt to realign cache buffers on allocation when quantized kernels are enabled.

kevin: Realignment helps but costs a memcpy on cache growth. Maybe heuristics: if average seq_len < 64 and quant kernels enabled, prefer aligned allocations; otherwise skip.

maria: Can we add a microbenchmark harness to isolate short-seq vs long-seq perf for each kernel variant? bench-bot, can you run 3 runs: seq=16,32,128 on a100 and h100 with per-head and per-tensor scales? Link results to the thread.

bench-bot: benchmark run queued: https://bench.redwood/s/5789 (will post numbers to thread when done).

aj: Last thought — fallback visibility: when runtime falls back from fused dequant to reference path, log a structured event with fields: kernel_requested, kernel_used, reason (mismatch/unaligned/unsupported-format), perf_estimate_delta. That'll make root-cause easier in CI.

kevin: I can sketch the ABI + small perf microbench tomorrow. Maria/Sara — want to pair on KV reallocation heuristics?

maria: Yup, can do.

sara: Count me in. I'll also draft the kernel metadata fields and numeric-quality metrics.

aj: Thanks all — will watch bench link and the canary. If regressions show up we'll revert the canary and iterate on ABI/prologue optimizations. :thumbsup:
